sentences.text: Scientists know Leninia only from a partial skull found inside a limestone nodule. This fossil measures about 45 cm, implying the complete skull once stretched between 65 and 90 cm.

The maxillary dental groove is extremely shallow, reaching only 16 mm in depth. The eye socket contained a scleral ring made of 14 trapezoidal plates with crenulations on their inner edges. Because the scleral aperture makes up just 11.03% of the orbital area, the animal had reached full growth.

Although the parietal bones are crushed together, there is no evidence that the skull possessed a crest. The specific name stellans refers to the star-shaped suture between the frontal and parietal bones.
The name Leninia honors Vladimir Lenin indirectly, as the museum housing the fossils is located within the Lenin Memorial and Lenin school complex in Ulyanovsk.
The scleral ring consists of 14 trapezoidal plates with crenulations on their inner edges, a unique structure for this species.

The genus Leninia was first described by Fischer, Arkhangelsky, Uspensky, Stenshin, and Godefroit in 2013. The fossil specimen was discovered in 2012 on the banks of the Volga River near the town of Kriushi inside a limestone nodule.

Leninia represents one of the latest-living and most basal ophthalmosaurine ichthyosaurs. The large scleral ring and aperture suggest that ophthalmosaurines were specialized deep-divers with conservative ecological niches.
Leninia is classified as a basal ophthalmosaurine ichthyosaur. It belongs to the family Ophthalmosauridae and the subfamily Ophthalmosaurinae.
Leninia lived during the late Early Cretaceous, specifically the lower Aptian stage, in western Russia. This period occurred between 121.4 and 119.57 million years ago.
It is debated whether the transverse crushing of the skull was caused by geological forces or the animal's death.
